item.title: Pentagon moves to fire publisher and editor of Stars and Stripes
item.description: The Pentagon has given separation notices to both the publisher and the editor-in-chief of Stars and Stripes, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Iran on U.S. tariff threat: "Same bull, different bullies"
item.description: Next week, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is expected to announce what he calls the "toughest sanctions in history" on Iran. Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi said of the threat, "We have seen this movie before. Same bull, different bullies." CBS News' Courtney Kealy reports.

item.title: Kindergarten vaccine exemptions hit record 4.2%, CDC says
item.description: The CDC says the number of children exempted from vaccine requirements was up to 4.2%, an estimated 155,000 kids across the country, during the 2025-2026 school year. Dr. Michael Bigham, chief quality officer for Akron Children's Hospital, joins CBS News to discuss.

item.title: Reports of sexual assault in the military decline for third straight year: Pentagon
item.description: The review included data from an anonymous survey conducted every other year that asks service members whether they've been the victim of unwanted sexual conduct or harassment.

item.title: Trump front-and-center in South Carolina GOP Senate runoff as he stumps for Darline Graham
item.description: President Trump is stumping for Sen. Darline Graham in South Carolina on Friday night as GOP voters prepare for the Senate runoff election just days away. NOTUS senior congressional editor Deirdre Walsh and Wall Street Journal national politics reporter Ken Thomas join to discuss.

item.title: What to know about Prince Harry and Meghan Markle's U.K. return
item.description: Prince Harry and Meghan Markle are moving back to the U.K. after six years in California. CBS News royal contributor Amanda Foreman joins "The Takeout" to discuss what the homecoming could look like.

item.title: "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan" guests for Aug. 23, 2026
item.description: This week's guests include Dr. Mehmet Oz, Democratic Rep. Seth Moulton of Massachusetts and Republican Rep. Byron Donalds of Florida.

item.title: First week wraps in Tupac murder trial, defendant says he's worried for his family's safety
item.description: The trial of Duane "Keefe D" Davis wrapped up its first week Friday with Davis telling the judge that he has concerns about the safety of his family. Davis is accused of orchestrating the killing of rapper Tupac Shakur in 1996. CBS News' Katrina Kaufman reports.

item.title: Alfalfa sprouts recalled after E. coli, salmonella outbreak sickens dozens
item.description: An outbreak of E. coli and salmonella that has sickened dozens of people across 15 states has been linked to an alfalfa grower in Minnesota, federal health officials said Friday.

item.title: Congressional lawyers facing barrage of AI-generated bills filled with errors
item.description: Lawmakers and lobbyists are now using artificial intelligence to draft bills, but it turns out AI is currently terrible at the technicalities of federal law and regulations. Politico Congress tech reporter Owen Dahlkamp joins to discuss his recent article on the topic.

item.title: Where South Carolina's GOP Senate race stands amid Trump visit
item.description: President Trump will be in Myrtle Beach, South Carolina, on Friday night, campaigning for Sen. Darline Graham ahead of her GOP primary runoff. Nicholas Reynolds, politics reporter for the Post and Courier, joins "The Takeout" to unpack the state of the race.

item.title: Legal scholar says Lindsay Clancy trial is a "battle of the experts" as defense rests
item.description: The defense in the murder trial of Lindsay Clancy, a Massachusetts mother who admitted to killing her children, rested on Friday. CBS News legal contributor Jessica Levinson joins "The Takeout" to look at the day's testimony.

item.title: Latest on USS Lincoln as it heads home to San Diego
item.description: The USS Abraham Lincoln has left the Middle East and is cruising back to its home port of San Diego after a record-long deployment. CBS News' Charlie D'Agata has more.

item.title: Trump campaigning for Darline Graham after debate gaffe
item.description: President Trump is in South Carolina Friday night to campaign for Sen. Darline Graham as she continues her campaign for a full term in her late brother Lindsey Graham's Senate seat. CBS News' Nikole Killion reports.

item.title: Body of New York grandmother who went missing in Las Vegas found, sister says
item.description: The body of Alisa Goods, a New York grandmother who went missing while visiting Las Vegas, has been found after more than a week, her sister told CBS News' Alice Gainer.

item.title: What to know as Lindsay Clancy trial nears closing arguments
item.description: The defense rested Friday in Lindsay Clancy's murder trial for the killings of her three young children. CBS News' Shanelle Kaul reports on the case.

item.title: "Everything as it was": Explore the bedrooms of kids killed in school shootings
item.description: The families of nine school shooting victims opened their doors to Steve Hartman and photographer Lou Bopp, allowing them to document their children's bedrooms.

item.title: Trump says Iran "not ready to make the right deal" as U.S. turns to economic warfare
item.description: As Vice President JD Vance declares economic pressure "the most effective tool that we have," Iran seeks to show deepening trade ties with its neighbors.

item.title: Psychiatrist testifies that Lindsay Clancy told children "go to God"
item.description: The defense rested in Lindsay Clancy's murder trial Friday in Massachusetts. The prosecution has started calling rebuttal witnesses.

item.title: Supreme Court lets Trump's White House ballroom project continue for now
item.description: The Supreme Court on Friday temporarily allowed President Trump's White House ballroom construction to continue. CBS News chief legal correspondent Jan Crawford has the details.

item.title: USS Lincoln leaves Middle East after 9-month deployment as Trump ramps up economic pressure on Iran
item.description: The USS Washington arrived in the Middle East from Asia on Thursday and relieved the USS Lincoln after a nine-month deployment. The move comes as the Trump administration says it will unveil the "toughest sanctions" on Iran. CBS News' Margaret Brennan and Elliot Ackerman have more.

item.title: Sword attack at school in Sweden leaves 1 dead, police say
item.description: An 18-year-old with a sword attacked a school Friday in central Sweden, killing one person and seriously injuring at least two others.

item.title: 8/21: The Takeout with Major Garrett
item.description: USS Lincoln leaves Middle East after 9-month deployment; Supreme Court temporarily allows White House to continue ballroom construction.

item.title: Walmart to let shoppers use Apple Pay and other tap-to-pay methods
item.description: Walmart will let shoppers use tap-to-pay methods, including Apple Pay and Google Pay, beginning later this month.

item.title: People are scrambling to find wads of cash dropped all over American cities
item.description: Cash drop social media accounts have people racing to find money hidden across the country. Here's what's behind the viral videos.

item.title: Woman covertly filmed by Meta smart glasses raises privacy concerns
item.description: One woman is speaking out after she was secretly filmed, saying that technology like Meta's AI-powered smart glasses threatens personal privacy.

item.title: Court says prosecutor who subpoenaed Letitia James was unlawfully appointed
item.description: A federal appeals court said the top federal prosecutor in the Northern District of New York was unlawfully serving when he subpoenaed state Attorney General Letitia James.

item.title: National Weather Service confirms tornado struck N.Y.'s Atlantic Beach
item.description: The National Weather Service confirmed a tornado struck Long Island's Atlantic Beach Thursday evening. It's the first confirmed tornado in Nassau County since 2021.

item.title: Mom says postpartum psychosis made her feel like "such a monster"
item.description: As the trial of Lindsay Clancy brings renewed attention to postpartum psychosis, Haley Ashcom shares her experience with the dangerous condition.

item.title: USS Abraham Lincoln leaving Middle East after 9-month deployment
item.description: The aircraft carrier and its 5,000 crew members will return to San Diego after an approximately nine-month deployment.
